studies.title: Bring-up: Apertus 1.5 text policy, 70B start-up, multi-set validation
studies.answer: Yes: the stack trains Apertus 1.5 8B and 70B on Alps. 70B needs the checkpoint manager off (host OOM during the HF load) and no in-flight weight updates.
studies.question: Does the NemoRL + NeMo-Gym mcqa stack train Apertus 1.5 (8B and 70B) on Alps?
studies.finding: Yes. The text conversion matches the release (MedQA 59.2 vs 59.8). 70B start-up peaks at ~415-420 GB per node during the HF load, so it host-OOMs with the checkpoint manager on. Async 70B hung when a vLLM engine died during in-flight weight updates, so those are now off. The multi-set validation (MedQA, MedXpertQA, MMLU-Pro health) smoke test passed on 10-07.

studies.title: Apertus 1.5 RL recipe on AlphaMed (256 x 8 per step)
studies.answer: 70B gains 4 MedQA points (64.3 -> 68.8 by step 40), then plateaus; no weights were saved. 8B ran out of data at step 39.
studies.question: Does the Apertus 1.5 recipe (8 rollouts, clip .2/.28, no KL, lr 1e-6) raise MedQA on 8B and 70B?
studies.finding: 70B: MedQA 64.3 → 68.8 at step 40, then a plateau (+4 pt). No weights were saved because checkpointing was off. 8B: dynamic sampling used ~2 batches per step, so the epoch ran out at step 39.

studies.title: Apertus 1.5-8B, AlphaMed-matched (64 x 8, 300 steps): no-think, thinking, pass-rate filtered + KL
studies.answer: No knowledge gain: the +5-6 points are the boxed answer format. maj@16 and medbench stay flat.
studies.question: Does AlphaMed's recipe give Apertus 1.5-8B a real knowledge gain?
studies.finding: No. The +5-6 pt RL-validation gain is the boxed format: ungradeable answers fall from 9.2 % to 0.4 %, while maj@16 stays flat at 64 and medbench is flat. Thinking reaches 64.0 on RL validation (step 250) but medbench is still flat, apart from MMLU-Pro health +4.9 (~3 SE).

studies.title: Llama-3.1-8B control: KL, entropy bonus, dynamic sampling, adaptive entropy
studies.answer: The pipeline reproduces most of AlphaMed on Llama-3.1-8B (best 73.2 vs AlphaMed-8B 75.8), but token entropy collapses.
studies.question: Does the pipeline reproduce AlphaMed on its own base model, and what limits the gain?
studies.finding: Control: 60.4 → 71.5 at step 75. Token entropy collapses from 3.6 to 0.33 by step 50, and answer length later collapses too. Dynamic sampling at step 75 is the best trade-off: medbench MedQA 72.3 with IFEval kept. Adaptive entropy (target 0.5) reaches 73.2 at T 0.6, against 75.8 for AlphaMed-8B. A fixed entropy bonus does nothing at 0.001 and diverges at 0.005.

studies.title: 70B thinking + KL (Apertus 1.5) and Llama-3.1-70B
studies.answer: Start-up memory tests only; no results yet.
studies.question: Can 70B runs checkpoint on 10 nodes (MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2) and does 70B gain more?
studies.finding: Start-up memory tests from 10-06. Results not written up yet.

studies.title: Six recipes on three test sets (Llama-3.1-8B, --val-multi)
studies.answer: The gap to AlphaMed-8B is real (MedXpertQA 16-19 vs 25.0), and its faithful recipe does not close it.
studies.question: Is the gap to AlphaMed-8B real on MedXpertQA and MMLU-Pro health, and does its exact recipe close it?
studies.finding: The gap is real: MedQA 70-72.7, MedXpertQA 16-18.9 and health 60-63, against AlphaMed-8B's 75.9 / 25.0 / 66.9 in the same evaluation. The AlphaMed-faithful recipe does not close it, although faithful step 75 has the best medbench MedQA (73.5).

studies.title: CuratedQA data (174k MCQ from meditronfo_gptoss_v1)
studies.answer: 9x more MCQ data gives the best MedQA (73.6) but leaves MedXpertQA at ~17.6.
studies.question: Does 9x more MCQ data move MedXpertQA where AlphaMed19K does not?
studies.finding: MedQA 73.6 at step 125 is the best of all val-multi runs, but MedXpertQA stays at 17.6, below the AlphaMed-data runs. Continuing to the full first CuratedQA pass (step 485) or switching to AlphaMed after step 300 (3 passes) gains nothing: MedQA drifts to 70-72, MedXpertQA stays 16-19.

studies.title: Apertus 1.5-8B: SFT checkpoint (pre-RL) vs the release
studies.answer: No: the pre-RL SFT checkpoint learns mostly format; the release stays ahead everywhere.
studies.question: The released Apertus 1.5-8B (after Swiss AI's RL) gained only the boxed format from AlphaMed RL (a1-apertus8b). Does the SFT checkpoint its RL started from (longctx_iter_0004200) learn more, i.e. was the release's RL what left nothing to gain? Faithful recipe, 200 steps, three-set validation, paired with the release on the same recipe.
studies.finding: Done 16 Oct: the SFT checkpoint does not learn more medicine. RL val (strict boxed, T=1) MedQA/MedXpertQA/health: SFT 3675528 22.6/5.0/23.4 -> 56.6/13.2/49.0 (mostly format); release 3675535 55.1/10.7/47.9 -> 61.4/13.8/54.2. Greedy no-think medbench before -> after, MedQA/MedMCQA/PubMedQA/MXQ/MMLU-Pro/health/IFEval/ARC-C: SFT 55.1/52.9/75.5/12.1/33.4/45.7/75.0/47.6 -> 57.8/52.8/77.7/13.0/40.7/46.9/73.0/47.4; release 60.9/53.2/76.0/13.5/46.9/52.1/86.3/55.8 -> 60.8/54.4/75.8/13.7/48.1/51.8/87.2/55.1. SFT MMLU-Pro +7.3 is in calculation subjects (business +20, chemistry +15, engineering +11, math +9, physics +8); knowledge subjects flat (health +1.2, law, history, psychology ~0). Release stays ahead everywhere; its own (math/IF/code) RL is what moved it.

studies.title: Reward only when the answer ends at the box (AlphaMed's stated rule)
studies.answer: No effect: the end-of-answer reward rule does not explain the AlphaMed gap.
studies.question: AlphaMed rewards 1 only 'if the model's response ends with a correctly formatted boxed answer'; our grader takes the last \boxed{} with any text after it. Does the end-anchored reward (punctuation still allowed) change the faithful run? Offline: it removes 0-5 pt of reward (base 29.8 -> 27.5, entds s75 71.4 -> 66.6, faithful s300 and AlphaMed-8B unchanged), so expect little.
studies.finding: Done 15 Oct: no effect. llama8b-alphamed-faithful-end 3660603 (300 steps) tracks faithful 3601795/3604613 within noise: best MedQA 72.3 (s125) vs 72.4, MedXpertQA 19.1 (s300) vs 18.9 peak, health ~60 vs ~61; step-1 train reward 0.39 vs 0.45. The end-of-answer reward rule does not explain the AlphaMed gap (MedXpertQA 25.0).

studies.title: How the update is formed: gradient clipping and prompts per step
studies.answer: Neither unclipped gradients nor 128 prompts per step closes the gap (MedXpertQA ~19 vs 25.0).
studies.question: AlphaMed-8B also scores 5 points more on its own training questions (76.6 vs faithful s300 71.3, T=1), with no larger weight change; does unclipping the gradient (every faithful step is clipped at 1, norm 1.2-2.0) or 128 prompts per step (DeepScaleR) lift the training reward past ~0.65 and close the gap? Plus the T=0.6 run judged at T=0.6.
studies.finding: Done 11 Oct. Clipping is not it: clip5 3637148 best 72.3/18.6/61.6, noclip 3637151 71.2/19.1/60.2 (MedQA/MedXpertQA/health) vs faithful 72.4/18.9/62.0; same ~0.65 reward plateau. 128 prompts/step (p128 3637008) best epoch-1 MedQA of the faithful family, 73.9 at step 150, but MedXpertQA 18.9 unchanged; epoch 2 reward 0.73 on seen questions while answers run away (500 to 1,960 tokens) and validation falls. T=0.6 eval 3637010: the T=0.6 run is worse at its own temperature too (step 300 59.6/12.0/47.6, 15 % unboxed). AlphaMed-8B 75.9/25.0/66.9.

studies.title: Reproduce 'Rethinking MCQ for RLVR' (arXiv 2603.12826) best Llama-8B recipe: self-curated distractors (IDC)
studies.answer: Reproduced: self-curated distractors reach MedXpertQA 20.4 (paper 20.3), our best. Caveat: the gold answer is the shortest option 40% of the time.
studies.question: Does GRPO+RLOO on MedQA-train with distractors curated by Llama-3.1-8B itself (IDC, T=7) reproduce the paper's MedXpertQA 14.3 -> 20.3 (greedy), vs the same recipe on the original options (paper: 16.3)?
studies.finding: Done 13 Oct. Yes: greedy medbench MedXpertQA IDC s316 20.4 (paper 20.3) vs orig 14.4-15.2, best of all our runs (AlphaMed-8B 23.8); MedQA 71.9, IFEval/ARC kept, PubMedQA -4. Caveat: gold is the shortest option 40 % of the time (orig 23 %).

studies.title: DeepScaleR settings AlphaMed-8B was likely trained with (rollout T 0.6, full-vocab entropy, 2 updates)
studies.answer: No DeepScaleR setting closes the MedXpertQA gap (best 18.8 vs 25.0).
studies.question: AlphaMed-8B's config names a deepscaler2 workspace; does DeepScaleR's recipe (rollout temperature 0.6, exact entropy bonus 0.001, 2 updates/step) close the MedXpertQA gap?
studies.finding: Done 10-10. No variant closes the MedXpertQA gap: best 18.8 (exact entropy) vs faithful 18.9 and AlphaMed 25.0; full DeepScaleR MedQA 73.3; T=0.6 alone declines. 1-node twins match, ~20% slower, ~40% fewer GPU-h. In axis1_results (11 Oct).

studies.title: Grid over the settings AlphaMed does not report (lr x updates/step x KL)
studies.answer: Only lr 1e-6 works; no lr, updates-per-step or KL setting closes the gap (best 18.5 vs 25.0).
studies.question: Does a higher learning rate, fewer/more policy updates per step or dropping KL let the faithful recipe reach AlphaMed-8B on MedXpertQA?
studies.finding: Done 10-10. Only lr 1e-6 works; at 3e-6 every run peaks at step 25 then degrades, at 1e-5 all collapse (two stopped early). No setting closes the MedXpertQA gap (best 18.5 vs AlphaMed 25.0). Fig 6 of axis1_results.

studies.title: Axis 2 offline evals: medbench and hallucination bench of rubric-RL checkpoints
studies.question: MCQ, IFEval and hallucination/over-refusal checks of the axis 2 checkpoints and their bases.

studies.title: Axis 1 offline evals: medbench, pass@k, format checks, consolidation
studies.question: Evaluation and analysis jobs that support the axis 1 runs.

studies.title: Rubric reward smoke tests
studies.answer: Yes, after two fixes (10-08).
studies.question: Does the healthbench_rubric Gym server with a Plumb-4B judge run inside GRPO?
studies.finding: Yes, after two fixes. Third smoke test on 10-08.

studies.title: Best axis-2 recipe on Apertus (MeditronFO 8B/70B, Apertus 1.5-8B)
studies.answer: Evolving rubrics with the Gemma-4 judge help both Apertus 8B models: Apertus 1.5-8B HealthBench .330 -> .491 (largest axis-2 gain), MeditronFO-8B .421 -> .466. The 70B smoke test trains and saves; the full 70B run is not launched.
studies.question: Evolving rubrics with the Gemma-4 judge (the best Llama-8B run) on Apertus MeditronFO: does the 8B gain where the old reward made it worse, and can a 70B run train and save weights for the evals?
studies.finding: 10-18: apertus8b-meditronfo-moove-rubric-drtulu-gemma (2 nodes, 200 steps, judge 2 nodes) and a 70B smoke test apertus70b-meditronfo-moove-rubric-drtulu-gemma-smoke (2 vLLM + 8 training nodes, async, checkpointing on without optimizer state, 4 steps, save every 2) launched. 10-19 results (HealthBench graded by Gemma-4 = the reward judge). MeditronFO-8B 3692149 (to step 120, walltime) resumed as 3695805 (200 steps): val MOOVE .36 -> .56, HB .34 -> .38, answers 1,670 -> 910 tok (no collapse, unlike the Plumb + length run); HB .421 -> .466 full, Pro .293 -> .310, AutoMOOVE vs its SFT start 53.7%, MedQA 61.2 (60.6), MedXpertQA 14.7 (13.7), IFEval 44.9 (40.1), over-refusal .12 -> .29, harmful refusal .72 -> .83, hallucination .96 (.96). Apertus 1.5-8B text, lr 5e-6, 3694599 (after two template-fix relaunches, listcontent chat template): learns this time, val MOOVE .55 -> .63, HB .32 -> .40, answers grow 335 -> 810 tok; HB .491 full / .363 Pro (highest of any axis-2 run; released untrained Apertus 1.5-8B .330 / .228, so +.16 / +.14), AutoMOOVE vs untrained 84.8%, MedQA 62.2 (60.9), MedXpertQA 13.4 (13.5), IFEval 86.9 (86.3), but benign over-refusal .58 (untrained .58: not from training), harmful refusal .91 (.92), hallucination .83 (.88). 70B: three load tests failed, smoke2 3693010 (10 nodes, 4 steps, 1h17) completed and saved; full 70B run not launched.

studies.title: Axis 2 on an MoE: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (between the 8B runs and Chonk)
studies.answer: The Megatron path works end to end on an MoE. One epoch at lr 1e-6 gives a modest gain (HealthBench .531 -> .554, AutoMOOVE 69%) with no regressions.
studies.question: Does the best axis-2 recipe (evolving rubrics, Gemma-4 judge) train an MoE (30B total, 3B active) the way it trains Llama-8B, and does the Megatron backend that Chonk will need work end to end (train, save, convert, evals)?
studies.finding: 10-19: Megatron config (TP 1, async: 1 vLLM node of four TP-1 engines + 4 training nodes; colocated ruled out: TP-1 engines would park ~230 GB of weights per node in host memory). Smokes on judge 3698566: EP 4 with KL 0.001 OOM (host) in the first reference log-prob pass (3698729, 3699669, 3700089); KL 0 trains, saves and converts to HF (3699748, weights match the original to ~1e-6); EP 16 with KL 0.001 trains at 171-193 GB per node (3700280). Steps judge-bound: training 4-8 s of 140-195 s (16 prompts, 1 judge node). Full run (5 + 3 judge nodes, a0238): 3700705 steps 1-30 eager, no in-flight updates, ~190-260 s/step, GPU util 18 %; debug smokes: CUDA graphs + in-flight updates ~1.8x answers/s (3701396), trajectory age 2 no gain (3701397); resumed with both from step 30 as 3701727: ~115-150 s/step, judge 70-74 % busy. Stopped at step 118: the async collector ends at one epoch (7,635 prompts / 64) and the job fails without converting. Validation reward flat (.529 -> .541 at step 90) while answers grew 895 -> 1,004 tokens; lr 1e-6 likely too low (Apertus needed 5e-6). 10-20: step_110 converted (3705485) -> evals 3701728-3701731 (moved to a0238). 10-20 results vs untrained Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 (HealthBench graded by Gemma-4 = the reward judge): HB .531 -> .554 full, Pro .337 -> .366; AutoMOOVE vs untrained 69.3% (346 wins, 106 ties, 124 losses of 576); MedQA 85.4 (85.6), MedXpertQA 25.3 (24.0), MedMCQA 71.9 (72.1), MMLU-Pro 71.7 (72.0), IFEval strict 83.2 (83.0); hallubench unchanged: pokemon hallucination .99 / 1.00 (same), MedSafetyBench fully refused .89 (.90), OR-Bench hard over-refusal .63 (.65), toxic refusal .97 (.97). Modest gain from one epoch at lr 1e-6, no regressions.

studies.title: What the consensus criteria add to evolving and per-question rubrics
studies.answer: Consensus criteria buy HealthBench full +.04 and safer, shorter answers, at 2-5 MedQA points. Evolving items recover most of that for AutoMOOVE without costing HealthBench Pro.
studies.question: DR Tulu (drtulu-gemma) scored on the 13 merged consensus criteria plus up to 5 evolving items; the per-question runs (persample-gemma) on their own rubric alone. How much of each run's result comes from the consensus criteria?
studies.finding: 10-18: two Gemma-4-judged ablations launched. drtulu-noconsensus-gemma: training groups on the evolving items alone, DR Tulu's score (sum / max(positive points, 5), unclipped); validation still on consensus. persample-merged-gemma: per-question rubric + merged consensus at 5 points each (build --variant persample+merged, ~23 criteria), validation on the per-question rubric only. persample-merged-gemma 3689921 done (200 steps, 6h50, val ~520 tok vs ~1,750 for persample-gemma): HB .422 full / .290 Pro (persample-gemma .382 / .320), AutoMOOVE vs Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 81.9% (33.2%), MedQA 71.3 (73.0), IFEval 72.6 (64.3), over-refusal .10 (.03), harmful refusal .69 (.58), hallucination .64 (.80). Consensus keeps answers short and safe, lifts HB full and AutoMOOVE, costs HB Pro. drtulu-noconsensus-gemma 3689920 done (200 steps, 9h, val 600 -> ~350 -> ~750 tok): HB .374 full / .270 Pro (drtulu-gemma .419 / .346), AutoMOOVE 82.2% (85.6%), MedQA 73.4 (68.1), IFEval 72.3 (68.6), over-refusal .08 (.17), harmful refusal .63 (.71), hallucination .65 (.60). Both directions agree: consensus = HB full +.04, more harmful-prompt refusal, less hallucination, shorter answers, at 2-5 MedQA points and more over-refusal. HB Pro differs: consensus helps the evolving run (+.08) but costs the per-question one (-.03). 10-19: persample-drtulu-gemma launched: per-question rubric as DR Tulu's persistent layer + up to 5 evolving items (+/-5, ~<=40% of the 37.4 positive points), no consensus, validation static. Last cell of {consensus, per-question} x {static, evolving}; vs persample-merged-gemma: does evolving do what consensus did (short, safe answers) while keeping the physician-derived items dominant? Judge 3694437 (a0238, 2 nodes). Result 10-19: 3694624 (to step 140) resumed as 3696832, stopped at step 151 by the 3-epoch cap, final = step 150: val MOOVE .33 -> .47, HB .24 -> .37, answers 590 -> ~1,220 tok (persample-gemma ~1,950 at s170; evolving items slow the length growth but do not stop it). HB .431 full (best Llama run) / .341 Pro (persample-gemma .382 / .320, drtulu-gemma .419 / .346), AutoMOOVE 75.1% (persample-gemma 33%, persample-merged 82%), MedQA 71.8, MedXpertQA 17.5, IFEval 64.5, over-refusal .02, harmful refusal .53, hallucination .76. Evolving items recover most of what consensus did for AutoMOOVE without costing Pro.

studies.title: Gemma-4-31B instead of Plumb-4B as the rubric judge
studies.answer: Yes: with Gemma-4 judging, answers no longer blow up, and DR Tulu becomes the best axis-2 Llama run (HealthBench .419 / Pro .346, AutoMOOVE 86%).
studies.question: With Plumb-4B grading, aspects-nolen answers grow to 1,750 tokens with errors left in, and DR Tulu games the judge (Plumb .41 -> .85 while Gemma-4 falls .42 -> .31). Does a judge at physician level change what the policy learns?
studies.finding: 10-16: Gemma-4 asked the reward's one-token A/B question (letter logits): HealthBench meta-eval macro F1 .673 (physicians .672, Plumb .636, Gemma explained verdict .698), 33.7 calls/s per node; calibration temperature 15. Two runs, judge on 2 nodes each (a0238): llama31-8b-moove-rubric-aspects-nolen-gemma and llama31-8b-moove-rubric-drtulu-gemma (Gemma also writes the evolving rubrics). 10-17 results (final checkpoints; HealthBench graded by Gemma-4, the reward's family): aspects-nolen-gemma 3678073 (6h18): no length blow-up (val 600 -> ~190 -> ~275 tok; Plumb 1,750), HB .354 full / .261 Pro (Plumb .276 / .268), AutoMOOVE vs Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 67.9%, MedQA 70.0, IFEval 73.8, hallucination .74 (Plumb .87), benign over-refusal .14 (.05). drtulu-gemma 3678074 (8h08): val length 268 -> 603 at s200 (Plumb 1,900), HB .419 full / .346 Pro (.316 length-adjusted; best axis-2 run; Plumb DR Tulu .380 / .269), AutoMOOVE 85.6%, MedQA 68.1, MedXpertQA 16.9, IFEval 68.6, hallucination .60, over-refusal .17 (untrained .59 / .28). Report: tech_reports/axis2_results.tex section "Gemma-4 instead of Plumb-4B as the judge".

studies.title: Rubric design: one HealthBench theme per question vs criteria grouped by aspect
studies.answer: One theme and aspects both collapse to one-line answers under the length term. DR Tulu's evolving rubrics without it is the best design (HealthBench .380); per-question rubrics give the best Pro (.271) but very long answers.
studies.question: Merging the consensus criteria of every theme that applies gives ~13 criteria per question, ~7 of them checking factual accuracy (53% of the reward). Does training on one theme per question (as HealthBench does), or on the same criteria weighted so that each aspect counts once, avoid the short one-template answers of the merged run?
studies.finding: Both collapse to one-line answers like the merged run (Llama, 200 steps, length term kept, ICRC out; 3636913 / 3636914, 10-11). Own validation .24 -> .81 (one theme) and .30 -> .90 (aspects). Checkpoint checks on the same 64 questions, all merged criteria: tokens 648 -> 79 / 79; Gemma-4 .42 -> .51 (one theme, step 50) / .58 (aspects, step 60). Aspects beat one theme on every aspect but asking for context, but answers still contain errors (Jadelle as an IUD, garbled Portuguese). Shared by all three designs: the length bonus and a reference-free judge. Next: aspects without the length term, then question-specific content criteria. 10-14: DR Tulu's evolving rubrics (Gemma-4-31B writes up to 5 items per question from each group's answers, zero-spread items retired) on the merged rubric without length term: llama31-8b-moove-rubric-drtulu, judge 3660795. Done 10-15 (3664722): consensus-rubric val .39 -> .86, but answers dip to ~270 tokens (step 60) then grow to ~1,900 by step 200, as without length term before. Step-200 evals (10-15): HealthBench .380 full / .269 Pro (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct .222 / .202; aspects .273, aspects-nolen .276 full); AutoMOOVE unanimous-576 vs Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 484 wins / 51 losses / 41 ties; medbench MedQA 67.2, MedXpertQA 18.0, IFEval 69.9; OR-Bench toxic refusal .73, pokemon-drugs hallucination .89 brand / .88 generic. Best axis-2 Llama so far. 10-16: per-question rubrics written by Gemma-4-31B from each question's MOOVE physician reviews (HealthBench style, ~10 criteria, -10..+10): on 600 votes hidden from the generator they pick the physician's answer .655 vs .549 for the consensus rubric. Run llama31-8b-moove-rubric-persample (Llama, no length term, 6,270 questions). Results 10-17 (Gemma-4): no length term (3677976, stopped ~step 155 at 3 epochs, answers ~3,500 tokens) HealthBench .322 full / .271 Pro (best Pro so far), MedQA 72.9, but IFEval .56 and toxic refusal .50; with the HealthBench length term (-len, 3678855, 200 steps, ~500 tokens) .310 / .251, MedQA 70.9, toxic refusal .83, Pokemon-drug hallucination .95.

studies.title: MOOVE consensus-criteria rubric RL (Plumb-4B judge)
studies.answer: No: with Plumb-4B and the length term, Llama collapses onto one template and MeditronFO-8B gets worse (HealthBench .421 -> .342); Apertus 1.5 stays flat.
studies.question: Does a rubric reward built from MOOVE consensus criteria improve answers without reward hacking?
studies.finding: Llama-3.1-8B goes from .35 to .89 on validation, but it collapses onto one paragraph template and gives an unsafe dog-bite answer (don't wash the wound). Apertus 1.5-8B stays flat (.59 → .64) with low entropy (.76 vs Llama 4.07). 40-step tests with lr 5e-6 and with thinking are done. The length term ranks systems by length (ρ .68/.48 vs .93/.98 without it), so dropping it is proposed. 10-14: same run on the ICLR Apertus-8B MeditronFO (SFT) model launched (apertus8b-meditronfo-moove-rubric 3664777): val .41 -> .74 in 200 steps (flat to step 30), answers 1,655 -> ~200 tokens, so it learns where Apertus 1.5 stayed flat, but shrinks like Llama under the length term. Step-200 evals vs its SFT start (10-15): HealthBench .342 vs .421 full, .209 vs .293 Pro (worse); AutoMOOVE unanimous-576 215 wins / 255 losses / 106 ties (worse); medbench slightly up (MedQA 62.9 vs 60.6, MedXpertQA 15.1 vs 13.7, IFEval 54.0 vs 47.0); OR-Bench toxic refusal .94 vs .84; hallucination .94 / .88 vs .97 / .93.

studies.title: Meditron-CHUV DPO (CHUV physician votes, decontaminated) on top of MeditronFO
studies.answer: No: CHUV SFT + DPO makes MeditronFO-70B worse everywhere (AutoMOOVE 19% vs 80%, HealthBench .434 vs .493, MedQA 64.5 vs 71.3). The CHUV SFT step causes it; DPO at CHUV strength barely moves anything.
studies.question: Does the Meditron-CHUV DPO step, on its physician preference pairs with every eval question removed, improve MeditronFO?
studies.finding: 10-18: data = CHUV dpo-either-non-aggregated (8762 votes), minus AutoMOOVE eval questions (416 rows) and the MeditronFO benchmark decontamination (1479 moove_chuv + 3 HealthBench): 6864 rows, 2529 questions, no CHUV system prompt. As in CHUV, SFT first on its distillation set (3366 -> 2602 rows after the same decontamination; 1 epoch, lr 1e-5, batch 32), then DPO from it (lr 9e-7 constant, 2 epochs, beta 0.1, batch 320 as 10 pairs x 32 GPUs, padding-free). 70B from the released MeditronFO-70B (_16n), 8 nodes: SFT 3692045 -> DPO 3692117, evals 3692118-22 vs MeditronFO-70B. 8B runs cancelled (user, 10-18). 10-19 results vs MeditronFO-70B: AutoMOOVE 18.9% vs 80.4%; CHUV placement (+pre) -0.87 vs +0.08, PHC -1.14 vs +0.35; HB full .434 vs .493 (Pro equal .303); medbench no-think MedQA 64.5 vs 71.3; toxic refusal collapses (Health-ORSC .12 vs .46). SFT-only ~ SFT+DPO in placement: the short CHUV SFT answers cause it; DPO at CHUV strength (lr 9e-7, beta .1, 41 steps) barely moves anything.
